paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend: the battle at Jericho was the LORD's before anybody picked up a horn. When Joshua asked whose side the man with the sword was on, the answer was "Neither." He said, "I have now come as Commander of the LORD's army." Joshua didn't get a side to join. He got a Commander to follow, and the LORD said, "Behold, I have delivered Jericho into your hand" (Joshua 5:14, 6:2).

So why the strange plan? Because it left no room for Israel to say they did it themselves. No ladders, no battering rams, just marching, horns and one shout. And look at what the people were asked to do: show up, keep walking, and keep their mouths closed until Joshua said to shout. Obeying a plan you can't explain, day after day, is a muscle, friend, and I'm still building mine (Joshua 6:3-5, 6:10).

This matters for your own walk with God. When He gives you a word, the task isn't to figure out how it will work. The task is to trust the Commander and keep walking. Rahab shows it too, because the one who hid the spies is the one who was brought out safe, and the LORD was with Joshua (Joshua 6:17, 6:25, 6:27). So when the wall in front of you looks way too big, remember who's in command.
